reviews.comment: You have 4 quizzes. They are posted in advance. Some are lecture questions. Most are reading. Open the quiz during lecture when you are discussing a lecture question. Write. Go home use readings to finish other questions. Then, this class will simply be about 2 research essays and 1 presentation (of your essay!). Email Maise any questions, trust.

Geva is a cool guy. He rambles, and the class is hard but there is a cheat code - he has an associate managing the class. Recognize that she does the 'work': grading, communicating, scheduling, feedback. She also has her own slides from her class which are better so make sure you ask for them. Talk to her early on and she will get you to an A.

Dr. Geva is so knowledgable and knows how to keep the class engaged. Yes he does cold call but it isn't as scary as people think. He asked basic questions as long as you skim the text you are fine. I never enjoyed a class more and have never had to work so hard for a grade. He gives numerous amount of feedback and he wants everyone to do well.

This class is hard, harder than I thought. I ended up getting a grade lower than I expected and wanted but it's the class I learned the most in during my time at A&M. Dr Geva wrote so much of the original literature the field is based on but has humility and connects it to real situations easily
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Records classes and makes them available which is very helpful because the material is hard if you care about really learning it. He lets you submit drafts, which I recommend you do AND attend. Its probably not possible to get an A if you dont show willing unless youre like a genius. Good guy

The hardest class Ive ever taken but really pushed me to learn. I got so much out of it. Take it but be ready to work hard. Geva is hilarious, tells stories on the edge of what he probably should talk about and has a great sense of humor. When his assistant sint there its chaos and worth watching.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He lectures and coldcalls BUT it's worth it for the class. You will learn history, politics and geography plus the psyhology and international relations. He is hilarious - dry humor and will "fight" with Maisie in class for his own fun which is cool because they are both really knowledgable so you learn a lot when they talk

Class was 2 papers, 3 quizzes, 1 presentation. Lectures were a lot of rambling, hard to take notes because slides were so blank. Not a super difficult grader, just looking to see that you put effort into your work. Attendance is not mandatory. Overall a good class to fill writing-intensive requirement. Helps you a lot in office hours

Geva was a great professor. He was very funny and laid back. He wanted everyone to do well in his course and tests weren't difficult and he gave review points. Lectures were a little ramble-y but attendance wasn't mandatory and he didn't care if you were on your phone every so often. Would absolutely take another class with him.

For a writing-intensive, this class was fine. Lectures were super hard to follow, and I'm pretty sure I learned nothing in them. The papers weren't too bad and he provides a ton of feedback on them. He doesn't give the papers back, so you have to guess your grade, which is annoying. Take home quizzes were easy, and you don't have to read for them.

His class was easy, but I felt like it was a waste. He didn't care about attendance and pretty much gave you an A on assignments if you turned them in. He's just an extremely boring lecturer. He's so knowledgeable that I think he forgets that he's talking to his students and not up in his office contemplating the ills of the world.

I took an undergraduate research course with Dr. Geva, but he typically teaches Foreign Policy Decision Making and Research Methods. He's a brilliant guy who genuinely cares for his students and is always willing to work with you if something comes up. Very knowledgeable, and always ready to point students to a great and relevant paper.

Textbook is honestly optional, depends on if you want to attend every lecture. Lets you submit drafts of both papers for feedback from both the TA and Geva himself. Geva is very understanding and will work with you on anything that comes up. Lectures were interesting and easy to follow.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Geva is great. He's got a little bit of an accent though, so if that's a no go for you don't take him. Only grades are a midterm and final, with sporadic written assignments that vary in difficulty from taking an easy 10 min to a paper that is quite extensive. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't skip you'll make an easy A or B.
He cares a lot about you!

I really liked Dr. Geva, but his lectures tended to drag since he went off-topic a lot. It  was hard at times to follow his train of thought, but I wrote down almost everything he said & that definitely helped me with the tests. He's great though with helping students write reports & he gives the class a chance to ask questions.

Lectures are slide-based and pretty boring. Grades consist of 2 tests, 2 papers, and 2 data collection assignments. The tests were not very difficult, but he does grade the papers pretty critically, but allows you to submit them earlier for feedback. He is also unclear in explaining how to write the papers. He is personable and funny though.
Great Professor! Really cares whether or not you learn. Two research papers, two short 2 page assignments and 2 tests. Would definitely take another class from him.

Fantastic professor. This was a writing intensive class that had 2 essays (~4 pages each), 2 short reports (1-2 pages each), and 2 MC exams. He gives you a list of things to study for the exams and asks nothing that's not on it. He will accept any paper as many times as you want to submit it so you're practically guaranteed an A in the class.
